section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: Debate 1: Multimodal Clinical Data Moat vs. Traditional Genomic Labs — Is Tempus an AI Software Platform or a Testing Lab?
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Bulls argue Tempus is fundamentally an AI data compounding engine, not a commodity diagnostics lab. Every genomic assay sequenced feeds into a proprietary library of over 7+ million de-identified patient records, creating an unmatched multimodal dataset that 19 of the top 20 oncology biopharma companies license to accelerate clinical trial recruitment and drug discovery. Bears counter that 67% of revenue still comes from diagnostic testing, where reimbursement pressures, lab overhead, and raw sequencing costs cap operating margins below pure-play software multiples.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: Analyst Focus Question: 'What percentage of your biopharma clients are expanding their annual data contract values into multi-year recurring subscriptions, and how is the gross margin on data licensing evolving relative to your clinical genomics business?'

section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: Debate 2: High Short Interest (25% of Float) vs. Operating Leverage Inflection — Will Breakeven Trigger a Short Squeeze?
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Bulls highlight that with 24.95% of float sold short, TEM has one of the highest short-interest concentrations in the Russell 2000 / mid-cap tech index. Short sellers have historically bet on persistent cash burn and high post-IPO share lockup dilution. However, with Q2 2026 operating cash burn dropping to -$7.53M and GAAP net income turning positive to $5.64M, bulls contend that any top-line beat-and-raise will ignite a violent short-covering rally toward the Street high target ($100.00). Bears argue the stock at $73.00 trades at ~9.3x sales for an unprofitable biotech asset.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: Analyst Focus Question: 'Given that your operating cash flow approached breakeven in Q2, do you anticipate generating positive operating cash flow during the second half of 2026 without any external financing?'
